property_summary: For every admin-invoked setOwner(newOwner) call, the contract's public owner equals the provided newOwner (reference preserves assignment); the mutant that inserts an intermediate owner = address(0) can cause owner to be address(0) after the call for some fuzzed inputs (when admin/owner interplay exposes the reset), violating the rule.

For any caller who is the admin, calling setOwner(x) results in C.owner() being equal to x after the call; the mutant that inserts owner = address(0) before assigning _owner can cause the post-call owner to be address(0) for some fuzzed inputs (when caller identity or fuzzed address interacts with admin/owner values), violating this property.

For any address newOwner and any actor who is the admin, after calling setOwner(newOwner) the public owner getter must return an address that is not the zero address (the reference never leaves owner as zero after a successful admin setOwner; the mutant that writes owner = address(0) before assigning can—under some caller/address relationships—leave owner observed as zero), so assert that c.owner() != address(0).

For every address newOwner and any admin caller, calling setOwner(newOwner) results in c.owner() == newOwner (the reference always sets owner to the provided value); the mutant that inserts owner = address(0) before assigning can cause c.owner() to be address(0) for some fuzzed newOwner, violating this equality.

For any admin caller and any _owner, if the admin calls setOwner(_owner) successfully then immediately reading the public owner getter yields a value that equals the provided _owner, but the mutant that inserts an extra owner = address(0) write before the assignment can (for some fuzzed admin/_owner combinations and caller ordering) produce a post-call owner that is address(0) instead of the provided _owner.

Invariant: only the original admin (the deployer) can change owner via setOwner, so after any call to setOwner by any caller other than the deployer the owner remains equal to the deployer; the mutant that makes onlyAdmin check owner instead of admin allows a non-admin (the current owner) to change owner and thus can produce a different owner for some inputs.

For every caller address X and target address Y, when X calls setOwner(Y) on the correct contract, the owner becomes Y only if X is the original admin (deployer); the mutant that checks owner instead of admin allows the current owner (not necessarily the original admin) to change owner, so there exist fuzzed X,Y where the mutant results in a different owner than the correct contract.

For all callers addrCaller and target owner addrNew, only the original admin (the deployer) can successfully change C.owner via setOwner; the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner instead of admin lets the current owner (which can be changed by non-admin in the mutant) perform changes that the original admin-only rule would not permit, so there exist addrCaller and addrNew where the mutant's resulting owner differs from the reference.

For every caller A and target newOwner B: if A is not the original deployer (admin), then calling setOwner(B) must NOT change owner (i.e., owner remains the deployer) — the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner instead of admin allows a non-admin who happens to be the current owner to change owner, so there exist fuzzed A,B where the mutant yields a different owner than the reference.

For every caller addrCaller and target addrNew, if addrCaller is not the original admin (the deployer), then calling setOwner(addrNew) must NOT change owner (owner stays the deployer); the mutant that checks msg.sender == owner instead of admin allows a caller who happens to be the current owner to change owner, so there exist addrCaller/addrNew that make the mutant produce a different owner than the reference.
